newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 pushed up by SPT Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 pushed up by SPT Telecom.

text.p: The Czech PX50 recovered from early losses on Monday boosted by the index's most heavily capitalised share SPT Telecom which rose 50 crowns, 1.3 percent, to 3,850.
The PX50 index rose 0.4 pct to 603.5 while the RPIX index of continuosly traded shares was up 0.5 percent to 1,283.4.

SPT has risen by more than 12 percent in the last two weeks driven, dealers say, by a wave of new confidence in the Czech equities market which has often been condemned for its lack of transparency and inadequate protection for small shareholders.
In recent weeks, bourse officials have become more and more vocal in their calls for immediate legislative improvements.

"On this positive wave (of high level calls for reform) a lot of domestic speculators were trying and succeeding, to make money...I think that the move of SPT Telecom entirely falls into this category," said Radek Vavra of Citicorp Securities.
"Generally, there is no fundamental reason for SPT's rise over the last two weeks," he added.

Analysts said that this weekend's world trade organisation agreement, which the Czech Republic and 67 other countries signed, to liberalise the global telecommunications market would have no short or medum-term effect on SPT's shares.
